title: Собеседование и резюме / Job interview and resume
bridge: In Russian, unlike Spanish, the verbs 'tener' and 'haber' do not exist. To express possession or experience, constructions with the verb 'у' (u) + genitive are used, such as 'у меня есть' (u menia yest') for 'I have'. Additionally, verbal aspect (perfective/imperfective) is fundamental: 'работал' (rabotal) indicates a past action without specifying if it was completed, while 'поработал' (porabotal) indicates completion. When talking about your resume, the perfective aspect is commonly used for completed actions, but the imperfective for general responsibilities. Be careful not to transfer the use of the Spanish present perfect tense: in Russian, the simple past is used for both nuances.
rule: To talk about your work experience in Russian in the context of a job interview, you need to master two key points: 1) The possession construction with 'у' + genitive for 'to have': 'у меня есть' (I have), 'у меня был/была/было' (I had). 2) Verbal aspect: to describe completed actions relevant to your application, use the perfective aspect (prefixes like по-, про-, от- or suffix -ну-). To describe habitual actions or ongoing processes, use the imperfective. Additionally, verbs of movement and state change are important: 'работал' (I worked/worked), 'окончил' (I graduated), 'получил' (I received). Remember that Russian has no articles and adjectives agree in gender, number, and case with the noun. When discussing your resume, it is advisable to use perfective verbs to list achievements (например: 'разработал проект' – I developed a project) and imperfective verbs to describe functions (например: 'отвечал за клиентов' – I was responsible for clients).

concept_examples.text: У меня есть пять лет опыта работы в маркетинге.
concept_examples.translation: I have five years of work experience in marketing.
concept_examples.phonetic: [u mʲɪˈnʲa jesʲtʲ pʲatʲ lʲet ˈopɨtə rɐˈbotɨ v mərkʲɪˈtʲinɡʲe]

concept_examples.text: В прошлом году я окончил университет по специальности экономика.
concept_examples.translation: Last year I graduated from university in economics.
concept_examples.phonetic: [f ˈproʂləm ˈɡodʊ ja ɐˈkonʲt͡ɕɪl ʊnʲɪvʲɪrˈsʲitʲet pə spʲɪt͡sɨˈalʲnəstʲɪ ɪkɐˈnomʲɪkə]

concept_examples.text: Я ищу работу, потому что хочу развиваться в своей области.
concept_examples.translation: I am looking for a job because I want to grow in my field.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja iˈɕːu ˈrabotʊ pɐˈtomʊ ʂtə xɐˈt͡ɕu rəzvʲɪˈvat͡sə f svɐˈjej ˈobləsʲtʲɪ]

concept_examples.text: На собеседовании меня спросили о моих сильных сторонах.
concept_examples.translation: At the interview, they asked me about my strengths.
concept_examples.phonetic: [nə səbʲɪˈsʲedəvənʲɪɪ mʲɪˈnʲa ˈsprosʲɪlʲɪ ə mɐˈix ˈsʲilʲnɨx stɐˈronəx]

common_error.wrong: Я имею опыт работы в продажах.
common_error.correct: У меня есть опыт работы в продажах.
common_error.correct_alt: У меня имеется опыт работы в продажах.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, we say 'yo tengo experiencia', so Spanish speakers tend to use the verb 'иметь' (imet') in Russian. However, in Russian, the construction 'у меня есть' (u menia yest') is more natural and correct to express possession or existence. 'Иметь' does exist, but it sounds formal or is used in specific contexts, such as 'иметь право' (to have the right). To avoid this mistake, internalize that existence/possession in Russian is expressed with 'у' + genitive.

examples.original: Меня зовут Анна, мне 28 лет.
examples.phonetic: [mʲɪˈnʲa zɐˈvut ˈanːə, mnʲe ˈdvətsətʲ ˈvosʲɪmʲ lʲet]
examples.translation: My name is Ana, I am 28 years old.
examples.note: For age, the structure 'мне + number + лет/года' is used. In Spanish it is 'tengo años', but in Russian the dative case is used.

examples.original: Я родилась в Испании, но сейчас живу в Москве.
examples.phonetic: [ja rɐˈdʲiləsʲ f ɪˈspanʲɪɪ, no sʲɪjˈt͡ɕas ˈʐɨvʊ v mɐskˈvʲe]
examples.translation: I was born in Spain, but now I live in Moscow.
examples.note: The verb 'родиться' is perfective and used in the past. It is 'родился' for masculine, 'родилась' for feminine. 'Жить' is imperfective and expresses current residence.

examples.original: Моя специальность - маркетинг, я работаю в этой сфере уже три года.
examples.phonetic: [mɐˈja spʲɪt͡sɨˈalʲnəsʲtʲ - ˈmarkʲɪtʲɪnk, ja rɐˈbotʲɪjʊ f ˈetəj ˈsfʲerʲɪ uˈʐɛ trʲi ˈɡodə]
examples.translation: My major is marketing, I have been working in this field for three years.
examples.note: Observe that 'уже' (already) is used to indicate duration up to the present. In Spanish 'desde hace' is used, but here the present tense plus 'уже' is used.

examples.original: У меня есть высшее образование и знание двух языков.
examples.phonetic: [u mʲɪˈnʲa jesʲtʲ ˈvɨʂɨje ɐbrəzɐˈvanʲɪje i ˈznanʲɪje dvux ɪˈzɨkəf]
examples.translation: I have higher education and knowledge of two languages.
examples.note: Review the possession construction 'у меня есть' with nouns in the nominative case. Here 'иметь' is not used.

examples.original: Я работал в компании три года и отвечал за продажи.
examples.phonetic: [ja rɐˈbotəl f kɐmˈpanʲɪɪ trʲi ˈɡodə i ɐtvʲɪˈt͡ɕæl zɐ prɐˈdaʐɨ]
examples.translation: I worked at the company for three years and was responsible for sales.
examples.note: Use of the imperfective aspect 'работал' to describe a duration. 'Отвечал за' is a common expression for 'responsible for'.

examples.original: В 2020 году я запустил новый проект, который принес прибыль.
examples.phonetic: [f dˈvʲe ˈtɨsʲɪt͡ɕɪ ˈdvad͡zətəm ˈɡodʊ ja zɐˈpusʲtʲil ˈnovɨj prɐˈɛkt, kɐˈtorɨj prʲɪnʲˈos prʲɪˈbɨlʲ]
examples.translation: In 2020 I launched a new project that brought profits.
examples.note: Here the perfective aspect 'запустил' is used because it is a completed action with a result. The year is in the prepositional case.

examples.original: Мои обязанности включали ведение переговоров с клиентами.
examples.phonetic: [mɐˈi ɐbʲɪˈzɐnːəsʲtʲɪ vklʲʉˈt͡ɕælʲɪ ˈvʲedʲɪnʲɪje pʲɪrʲɪɡɐˈvorəf s klʲɪˈjentəmʲɪ]
examples.translation: My responsibilities included conducting negotiations with clients.
examples.note: The verb 'включать' is imperfective and used to describe general functions. 'Ведение' is a verbal noun derived from 'вести'.

examples.original: Я получил повышение, потому что улучшил показатели отдела.
examples.phonetic: [ja pɐˈlʊt͡ɕɪl pəvɨˈʂenʲɪje, pɐˈtomʊ ʂtə ulʊt͡ʂˈʂɨl pəkɐˈzatʲɪlʲɪ ɐdʲˈdʲelə]
examples.translation: I received a promotion because I improved the department's performance indicators.
examples.note: Use of the perfective 'получил' for a specific event. The conjunction 'потому что' indicates cause, equivalent to 'because'.

examples.original: Я хотел бы найти работу с гибким графиком и возможностью удалённой работы.
examples.phonetic: [ja xɐˈtʲel bɨ nɐjˈtʲi ˈrabotʊ z ˈɡʲipkʲɪm ˈɡrafʲɪkəm i vɐzˈmoʐnəsʲtʲju ʊdɐˈlʲɵnːəj ˈrabotɨ]
examples.translation: I would like to find a job with flexible hours and the possibility of remote work.
examples.note: The particle 'бы' forms the conditional. 'Хотел бы' is the polite way to express desires. 'С' + instrumental is used for accompaniment.

examples.original: В ближайшие пять лет я планирую стать менеджером проектов.
examples.phonetic: [v blʲɪˈʐajʂɨje pʲatʲ lʲet ja plɐˈnʲirʊjʊ sˈtatʲ ˈmʲenʲɪd͡ʐərəm prɐˈɛktəf]
examples.translation: In the next five years I plan to become a project manager.
examples.note: 'Стать' + instrumental expresses 'to become'. The dative of time with 'в' + accusative is used for future duration.

examples.original: После собеседования я надеюсь получить ответ на следующей неделе.
examples.phonetic: [ˈposlʲe səbʲɪˈsʲedəvənʲɪjə ja nɐˈdʲejʉsʲ pɐˈlʊt͡ɕɪtʲ ˈotvʲet nə ˈslʲedʊjʉɕːɪj nʲɪˈdʲelʲɪ]
examples.translation: After the interview I hope to receive an answer next week.
examples.note: 'После' + genitive means 'after'. The verb 'надеяться' is used with the infinitive. For 'next week' the accusative with 'на' is used.

examples.original: Если я получу эту должность, я буду работать в международной команде.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲɪ ja pɐˈlʊt͡ɕʊ ˈɛtʊ ˈdoʐnəsʲtʲ, ja ˈbudʊ rɐˈbotətʲ v mʲɪʐdʊnɐˈrodnəj kɐˈmandʲe]
examples.translation: If I get this position, I will work in an international team.
examples.note: In real conditionals, the present tense (perfective 'получу') is used in the condition and future ('буду работать') in the consequence. Unlike Spanish, the subjunctive is not used.

title: Обсуждение текущих событий / Talking about news and current events
bridge: In Russian, to talk about current events, the verbal aspect (imperfective for ongoing or habitual actions, perfective for completed results) is frequently used. Unlike Spanish, where verb tenses (preterite, imperfect) mark the difference, Russian relies on verbal prefixes and suffixes. Additionally, Russian uses impersonal constructions with the dative to express opinions (Мне кажется, equivalent to 'It seems to me'), which is quite different from Spanish. Also pay attention to the use of the genitive case after numbers ('три новости' – 'three news items'), something that has no direct parallel in Spanish.
rule: To discuss news in Russian (B1 level), you should master: 1) Expressing opinions with verbs like 'считать' (to consider) and 'казаться' (to seem) in constructions with the dative (мне кажется) or with the instrumental (я считаю это важным). 2) The use of verbal aspects: imperfective to narrate or describe (читал, смотрел) and perfective for completed actions (прочитал, посмотрел). 3) Typical time expressions: 'недавно' (recently), 'вчера' (yesterday), 'сегодня' (today), 'на этой неделе' (this week). 4) The plural genitive case after numbers for nouns (e.g., 'три статьи' but 'пять статей'). 5) Speech verbs: 'сказать' (to say, perfective) and 'говорить' (to say, imperfective). 6) The structure of subordinate clauses with 'что' (that) to report information, similar to Spanish. At B1 level, you should be able to describe events, express your opinion, and react to news coherently, using around 10-15 sentences, with occasional errors that do not hinder communication.

concept_examples.text: Я недавно прочитал статью о выборах.
concept_examples.translation: I recently read an article about the elections.

concept_examples.text: По телевизору говорили о наводнении в Испании.
concept_examples.translation: They were talking on TV about the flood in Spain.
concept_examples.phonetic: [pə tʲɪlʲɪˈvʲizərʊ ɡəvɐˈrʲilʲɪ ɐ nəvɐdˈnʲenʲɪɪ v ɪˈspanʲɪɪ]

concept_examples.text: Мне кажется, что эта новость очень важная.
concept_examples.translation: It seems to me that this news is very important.
concept_examples.phonetic: [mnʲe ˈkaʐɨt͡sə ʂto ˈɛtə ˈnovəsʲtʲ ˈot͡ɕɪnʲ ˈvaʐnəjə]

concept_examples.text: Вчера состоялась пресс-конференция президента.
concept_examples.translation: Yesterday, the president’s press conference took place.

common_error.wrong: Я недавно читал статья о выборах.
common_error.correct: Я недавно читал статью о выборах.
common_error.correct_alt: Я недавно прочитал статью о выборах.
common_error.explanation: The main error is the case of the noun 'статья' (article). After the verb 'читать' (to read), the accusative case is used: 'статью' (not 'статья'). This is a typical mistake because in Spanish, the direct object does not require morphological changes, while in Russian, animate and inanimate nouns change their endings according to the case. Also note that 'недавно' (recently) often takes the perfective aspect (прочитал) if the action is completed, but the imperfective (читал) is valid if you describe a past action without specifying its completion. To avoid errors, always ask yourself: 'Is the action completed? Then use the perfective aspect.'

examples.original: Я считаю, что это решение правильное.
examples.translation: I consider that this decision is correct.
examples.note: The verb 'считать' (to consider) is used with the conjunction 'что' (that) and the adjective in the nominative case, similar to 'considerar que' in Spanish.

examples.original: По-моему, это очень серьёзная проблема.
examples.translation: In my opinion, this is a very serious problem.
examples.note: 'По-моему' is a common way to introduce an opinion, equivalent to 'in my opinion'. It is placed at the beginning of the sentence.

examples.original: Мне кажется, что ситуация скоро изменится.
examples.translation: It seems to me that the situation will change soon.
examples.note: The impersonal construction 'мне кажется' (it seems to me) requires the dative case (мне) and is followed by 'что' (that) with a complete clause.

examples.original: В новостях сказали, что завтра будет дождь.
examples.phonetic: [v nɐˈvostʲəx skɐˈzalʲɪ, ʂto ˈzaftrə ˈbudʲɪt doʂtʲ]
examples.translation: The news said that it will rain tomorrow.
examples.note: Observe the impersonal use of 'сказали' (they said) in the plural, similar to 'they said' in English, but in Russian it is used to refer to people in general.

examples.original: Правительство объявило о новых мерах.
examples.translation: The government announced new measures.
examples.note: The verb 'объявить' (to announce) is used with 'о + prepositional' to indicate the topic of the announcement.

examples.original: Я услышал по радио, что цены выросли.
examples.translation: I heard on the radio that prices have gone up.
examples.note: The verb 'услышать' (to hear, perfective) indicates that you completed the action of listening. It is used with 'по радио' (on the radio).

examples.original: Как ты думаешь, что произойдёт дальше?
examples.translation: What do you think will happen next?
examples.note: The structure 'как ты думаешь' (what do you think?) + indirect question with 'что'.

examples.original: Это очень интересно, но я не согласен с этим.
examples.phonetic: [ˈɛtə ˈot͡ɕɪnʲ ɪnʲtʲɪˈrʲesnə, no ja nʲɪ sɐˈɡlasʲɪn s ˈɛtʲɪm]
examples.translation: This is very interesting, but I don’t agree with this.
examples.note: To express disagreement, use 'я не согласен' (I don’t agree), followed by 'с + instrumental' to indicate what you disagree with.

examples.original: А что если это неправда?
examples.translation: What if this isn’t true?
examples.note: 'А что если' is an expression used to propose a hypothesis, similar to 'what if' in English.

translations.en: Talking about news and current events

title: Культурные различия и недопонимание / Cultural differences and misunderstandings
bridge: In Spanish, expressions of politeness and interpersonal distance vary greatly by region, but in Russian there are stricter norms: the use of 'ты' (informal 'you') and 'вы' (formal 'you') is crucial and depends on age, social status, and the formality of the context. Additionally, Russians tend to be more direct in conversation, which may come across as blunt or even rude to a Spanish speaker accustomed to more indirect language and polite circumlocutions. On the other hand, Russian does not have an exact equivalent of 'please' in imperatives: the simple imperative form is used with a polite intonation, whereas in Spanish we add 'por favor' or conditional structures like '¿podrías?'.
rule: In Russian, the choice between 'ты' (informal) and 'вы' (formal) is mandatory and affects verb conjugation and context. 'Ты' is used with friends, family, children, and people younger than the speaker; 'вы' is used with strangers, superiors, older people, and in formal situations. In the plural, 'вы' is always used when addressing multiple people. In imperatives, to make polite requests, the particle 'пожалуйста' (please) is placed at the beginning or end, but the verb form remains the simple imperative (дай, скажи, помоги). In Spanish, we tend to use conditionals or indirect questions ('¿me podrías...?'), which is not common in Russian: the imperative with a descending intonation is used instead. Another important point: in Russian, diminutive nicknames (like 'Маша' for 'Мария') are frequently used in intimate conversation but not in formal situations. To ask how someone is, 'Как дела?' is used (informal) or 'Как у Вас дела?' (formal), and the expected answer is usually 'Нормально' (fine/okay) rather than detailing as is common in Spanish.

concept_examples.text: Извините, вы не подскажете, где здесь метро?
concept_examples.translation: Excuse me, could you tell me where the metro is here?
concept_examples.phonetic: [ɪzˈvʲinʲɪtʲe, vɨ nʲɪ pɐtsˈkaʐɨtʲe, ɡdʲe zʲdʲesʲ mʲɪˈtro]

concept_examples.text: Ты не мог бы мне помочь?
concept_examples.translation: Could you help me? (informal, literally: 'Couldn’t you help me?')

concept_examples.text: Пожалуйста, передайте соль.
concept_examples.translation: Please pass me the salt (formal, addressing one person).

concept_examples.text: Как у Вас дела?
concept_examples.translation: How are your affairs? (formal, equivalent to 'How are you?')

common_error.wrong: ¿Podrías darme el libro? (using the conditional directly in Russian)
common_error.correct_alt: Не мог бы ты дать мне книгу?
common_error.explanation: A common mistake is to transfer the Spanish politeness of the conditional ('¿podrías...?') directly into Russian, but Russian prefers the simple imperative with 'пожалуйста' or the construction 'не мог бы (ты/вы) + infinitive' to be polite. Saying '¿Podrías darme el libro?' literally translated as 'Мог бы ты дать мне книгу?' sounds strange and unnatural. Russians use the imperative with a kind intonation, not with conditional structures. To avoid the error, remember that in Russian politeness is achieved through the choice of 'ты' vs 'вы' and the addition of 'пожалуйста', not through modal verbs.

examples.original: Ты говоришь по-русски?
examples.translation: Do you speak Russian? (informal)
examples.note: Use 'ты' with friends or young people. The verb conjugation is in the second-person singular.

examples.original: Вы говорите по-русски?
examples.translation: Do you speak Russian? (formal)
examples.note: Use 'вы' to show respect or distance. The conjugation is in the second-person plural, even when addressing one person.

examples.original: Можно на «ты»?
examples.translation: Can we switch to 'tú'? (literal: 'Can we go to 'you'?')
examples.note: A typical phrase to move to informal address. Used to avoid a cultural misunderstanding.

examples.original: Сделай это сейчас!
examples.translation: Do it now! (informal, direct imperative)
examples.note: In Russian, a direct imperative is not rude when used with friends. In Spanish, it sounds very blunt; that’s why Spanish speakers tend to add 'por favor' even in imperatives, but in Russian it can be omitted without being rude.

examples.original: Сделайте это, пожалуйста.
examples.translation: Please do this. (formal)
examples.note: The particle 'пожалуйста' softens the formal imperative. In Russian it is more common than in Spanish, but not used as frequently as in Spanish conditional requests.

examples.original: Не могли бы вы мне помочь?
examples.translation: Could you help me? (very polite, formal)
examples.note: This structure is the most polite way to ask for help, similar to the Spanish conditional, but used sparingly so as not to sound overly formal.

examples.original: Не спрашивайте о зарплате.
examples.translation: Do not ask about salary.
examples.note: Although generally taboo, in Russia salary can sometimes be discussed in confidence, but it is not polite in formal contexts. In Spanish it is also delicate, but there is more flexibility.

examples.original: Извините, я не хочу говорить о политике.
examples.phonetic: [ɪzˈvʲinʲɪtʲe, ja nʲɪ xɐˈt͡ɕu ɡɐˈvorʲitʲ ɐ pɐˈlʲitʲɪkʲe]
examples.translation: Sorry, I don’t want to talk about politics.
examples.note: Politics is a sensitive topic. If you don’t want to discuss it, it’s common to decline politely. Russians usually don’t insist if the other person excuses themselves.

examples.original: Угощение обязательно — попробуйте!
examples.translation: Offering food is mandatory — try some! (in a Russian home)
examples.note: In Russian culture, refusing food offered by the host can be offensive. In Spanish culture it’s also the case, but insistence may be less. If you’re on a diet, say 'Спасибо, я сыт' (Thank you, I’m full).

title: Обсуждение экологии / Talking about the environment
bridge: In Russian, impersonal constructions with «нужно» or «надо» + infinitive are used to express obligations or recommended actions in ecological contexts, while in Spanish we use 'hay que' or 'es necesario'. Additionally, the verbs «защищать» (to protect) and «сохранять» (to conserve) require accusative case objects, but the verb «заботиться» (to care for) is constructed with the instrumental case («о + prepositional»). Be careful with the use of «экология»: in Russian it refers to the environment as a field, but it is also used colloquially to talk about environmental issues.
rule: To talk about ecological actions at B1 level, use: 1) «нужно/надо/необходимо» + infinitive (impersonal, no subject): «Нужно сортировать мусор» (You must sort the trash). 2) Verbs with specific case requirements: «защищать что?» (accusative), «сохранять что?» (accusative), «заботиться о чём?» (prepositional with «о»), «экономить что?» (accusative: «экономить воду»). 3) Short adjectives: «важно» (it's important), «полезно» (it's useful), «вредно» (it's harmful) + infinitive. 4) To express personal opinion: «Я думаю, что...», «По-моему, ...». 5) Reflexive verbs with «-ся» are common: «загрязняться» (to become polluted), «перерабатываться» (to be recycled). Exception: «природа» is used with the preposition «в» (в природе), but «на природе» means 'outdoors'.

concept_examples.text: Нужно сортировать мусор, чтобы защитить природу.
concept_examples.translation: Hay que separar la basura para proteger la naturaleza.

concept_examples.text: Мы должны экономить воду и электричество.
concept_examples.translation: Debemos ahorrar agua y electricidad.

concept_examples.text: Важно заботиться о природе уже сейчас.
concept_examples.translation: Es importante cuidar la naturaleza ya ahora.

concept_examples.text: Пластик очень долго разлагается в природе.
concept_examples.translation: El plástico tarda mucho en descomponerse en la naturaleza.

common_error.wrong: Я забочусь природа (literal: yo cuido la naturaleza, error de caso)
common_error.explanation: The verb «заботиться» (to care for, to be concerned about) requires the preposition «о» + a noun in the prepositional case. Spanish speakers often directly transfer the structure 'cuidar + direct object' (accusative) to Russian, but in Russian, care is expressed with «о + prepositional». To avoid this error, memorize verbs that govern prepositions (заботиться о, думать о, беспокоиться о).

examples.original: Загрязнение воздуха — серьёзная проблема в больших городах.
examples.phonetic: [zəɡrʲɪzˈnʲenʲɪjə ˈvozdʊxə | sʲɪˈrʲjɵznəjə prɐˈblʲemə v bɐlʲˈʂɨx ɡɐˈrodəx]
examples.translation: La contaminación del aire es un problema grave en las grandes ciudades.
examples.note: The noun «загрязнение» governs the genitive case (воздуха). Note that in Spanish we use 'del aire'.

examples.original: Изменение климата влияет на погоду.
examples.translation: El cambio climático afecta al tiempo.
examples.note: «Влиять на + accusative» is used like 'afectar a'. Remember that in Russian the preposition 'на' indicates direction.

examples.original: Пластиковые отходы наносят вред океану.
examples.translation: Los desechos plásticos dañan el océano.
examples.note: «Наносить вред + dative» is a formal way to say 'to cause harm'.

examples.original: Мы стараемся покупать продукты без упаковки.
examples.translation: Intentamos comprar productos sin embalaje.
examples.note: «Без + genitive» indicates 'without something'. Note the use of «стараться» + infinitive.

examples.original: Я предлагаю использовать меньше пластика.
examples.translation: Propongo usar menos plástico.
examples.note: «Меньше» + genitive for 'less of'.

examples.original: Они собирают дождевую воду для полива растений.
examples.phonetic: [ɐnʲɪ sɐˈbʲirəjʊt dəʐˈdʲevʊjʊ ˈvodu dlʲə pɐˈlʲivə rɐˈsʲtʲenʲɪj]
examples.translation: Recogen agua de lluvia para regar las plantas.
examples.note: «Для + genitive» expresses purpose ('for').

examples.original: Нужно использовать общественный транспорт вместо машины.
examples.translation: Hay que usar el transporte público en lugar del coche.
examples.note: «Вместо + genitive» is equivalent to 'instead of'.

examples.original: Если мы не изменим свои привычки, климат ухудшится.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲi mɨ nʲɪ ɪzmʲɪˈnʲim svɐˈi prʲɪˈvɨt͡ɕkʲɪ | ˈklʲimət ʊˈxʊt͡ʂɨt͡sə]
examples.translation: Si no cambiamos nuestros hábitos, el clima empeorará.
examples.note: In Russian, real conditional sentences use present/perfective in the present with future in the apodosis (similar to Spanish).

examples.original: Я надеюсь, что люди начнут больше использовать возобновляемую энергию.
examples.phonetic: [jæ nɐˈdʲejʉsʲ | ʂtɐ ˈlʲudʲɪ nɐt͡ʂˈnut ˈbolʲʂə ɪspɐlʲzɐˈvatʲ vəzəbnɐˈvlʲæjɪmʊjʊ ɪˈnʲergʲɪjʊ]
examples.translation: Espero que la gente empiece a usar más energía renovable.
examples.note: «Надеяться, что» + subordinate clause. «Начать» (perfective) + infinitive.

examples.original: Мусор можно переработать и использовать снова.
examples.translation: La basura se puede reciclar y usar de nuevo.
examples.note: «Можно» + infinitive (impersonal) = 'can be'. «Снова» = 'again'.

examples.original: Каждый человек должен внести свой вклад в охрану природы.
examples.phonetic: [ˈkaʐdɨj t͡ɕɪˈvʲek ˈdolʐɨn vnʲɪˈsʲtʲi svoj fklat f ɐˈxranʊ prʲɪˈrodɨ]
examples.translation: Cada persona debe contribuir a la protección de la naturaleza.
examples.note: «Внести вклад в + accusative» = 'to contribute to'. «Охрана» governs the genitive case.

title: Технологии и социальные сети / Technology and social media
bridge: In Spanish, we use the present indicative ('publico', 'comparto') to express habitual actions, but in Russian, it is common to use the imperfective aspect with verbs of movement and action. Additionally, Russian verbs change form depending on the aspect (perfective/imperfective), which does not exist in Spanish. Be careful with declension: after prepositions like 'в' (in) or 'на' (on), the prepositional case is used, requiring specific endings (e.g., 'в интернете', not 'в интернет'). You will also notice that verb prefixes (like 'вы-' or 'за-') change the meaning, something that in Spanish is achieved with adverbs or different verbs.
rule: To talk about technology and social media in Russian at B1 level, use the imperfective aspect for ongoing or habitual actions (я читаю новости - I read the news), and the perfective aspect for completed actions (я прочитал статью - I have read the article). Verbs of movement like 'ходить' (to go habitually) and 'пойти' (to go once) are key. Prepositions 'в' and 'на' require the prepositional case (в интернете, на сайте) to indicate location, and the accusative case (в интернет, на сайт) for direction. Nouns ending in -а/я change to -е in the prepositional case (соцсеть -> в соцсети). To express 'I like', use 'нравится' with the dative case (мне нравится), not a reflexive verb as in Spanish. Include frequent adverbs: 'онлайн', 'офлайн', 'часто', 'редко'. Remember that perfective verbs are not used in the present tense; only the imperfective form is used.

concept_examples.text: Я часто публикую фото в Instagram.
concept_examples.translation: I often post photos on Instagram.

concept_examples.text: Ты уже прочитал моё сообщение?
concept_examples.translation: Have you already read my message?

concept_examples.text: Мы часто смотрим видео на YouTube.
concept_examples.translation: We often watch videos on YouTube.

concept_examples.text: Она выложила новую сторис.
concept_examples.translation: She posted a new story.

common_error.correct_alt: Я сижу в интернете каждый день.
common_error.explanation: The mistake occurs because in Spanish we say 'en internet' without changing the word. In Russian, after the preposition 'в' (in), the prepositional case is used, which for 'интернет' (masculine) is formed by adding -е. Additionally, with state verbs like 'сидеть' (to be sitting/ to be), the prepositional case is used. To talk about an action directed toward the internet, the accusative case would be used (я захожу в интернет - I go onto the internet). To avoid the mistake, remember: if you are inside something (a place), use the prepositional case; if you are going toward something, use the accusative case.

examples.original: Я выложил новое фото.
examples.translation: I have posted a new photo.
examples.note: The verb 'выложить' is perfective; it is used for completed actions. For habitual actions, use 'выкладывать' (imperfective).

examples.original: Она комментирует мои посты.
examples.translation: She comments on my posts.
examples.note: The verb 'комментировать' is imperfective and is used in the present tense. The plural of 'пост' (post) is 'посты' with the stress on the last syllable.

examples.original: Мы делимся новостями в чате.
examples.translation: We share news in the chat.
examples.note: The verb 'делиться' + instrumental (чем?) indicates what is being shared. Here, 'новостями' is in the instrumental plural.

examples.original: Напиши мне в WhatsApp.
examples.translation: Message me on WhatsApp.
examples.note: The verb 'написать' is perfective; it is used to give an order to complete the action. For a general order, use 'пиши'.

examples.original: Я отправил тебе файл.
examples.translation: I have sent you a file.
examples.note: The verb 'отправить' is perfective; the recipient is in the dative case (тебе).

examples.original: Ты получил моё голосовое сообщение?
examples.translation: Have you received my voice message?
examples.note: The verb 'получить' is perfective; in the present tense, 'получать' is used for habitual actions.

examples.original: Он не отвечает на мои сообщения.
examples.translation: He does not respond to my messages.
examples.note: The verb 'отвечать' is imperfective; 'на' + accusative indicates what is being responded to.

examples.original: Я провожу много времени в интернете.
examples.translation: I spend a lot of time online.
examples.note: The verb 'проводить' (imperfective) is used for habitual actions. In the prepositional case, 'интернет' changes to 'интернете'.

examples.original: Ты часто заходишь в ТикТок?
examples.translation: Do you often go onto TikTok?
examples.note: The verb 'заходить' is imperfective and is used with 'в' + accusative to indicate direction.

examples.original: Мы редко смотрим телевизор, мы смотрим стримы.
examples.phonetic: [mɨ ˈrʲetkə ˈsmotrʲɪm tʲɪlʲɪˈvʲizər, mɨ ˈsmotrʲɪm ˈstrʲimɨ]
examples.translation: We rarely watch TV, we watch streams.
examples.note: The adverb 'редко' (rarely) usually comes before the verb. 'Смотрим' is imperfective and is used for habitual actions.

examples.original: Он каждый день проверяет новости.
examples.translation: He checks the news every day.
examples.note: The expression 'каждый день' (every day) is used with the imperfective aspect for routines. 'Проверять' is imperfective; the perfective form would be 'проверить'.

title: Образование и учёба за границей / Education and studying abroad
bridge: In Russian, to talk about studying abroad, the verb 'учиться' (to study, to be a student) is used with the preposition 'за' + instrumental case ('за границей', 'за рубежом'). Unlike Spanish, where 'estudiar' can be intransitive or transitive, in Russian 'учиться' requires a prepositional or accusative complement to indicate the institution ('учиться в университете', 'учиться на курсах'). Additionally, verbal aspect is crucial: 'поступить' (to enter, perfective) and 'поступать' (imperfective) are used in different contexts, and Spanish speakers often confuse them. Also pay attention to case usage: after 'поступить' the accusative case is used ('в университет'), but to say 'to study at' the prepositional case is used ('в университете').
rule: To express 'to study abroad' the construction 'учиться за границей' or 'учиться за рубежом' is used. The verb 'учиться' conjugates as follows: я учусь, ты учишься, он/она учится, мы учимся, вы учитесь, они учатся. To say 'to study at an institution' use 'учиться в + prepositional' (в школе, в университете, в институте) or 'на + prepositional' (на курсах, на факультете). To say 'to enter a university' use 'поступить в + accusative' (в университет, в институт, в школу) or 'на + accusative' (на курсы, на факультет). The imperfective 'поступать' is used for repeated or ongoing actions. 'Учиться на...' is also used to indicate a major: 'учиться на инженера' (to study to be an engineer). For 'scholarship' use 'стипендия', and for 'exchange' use 'обмен' (студенческий обмен).

concept_examples.text: Я хочу учиться за границей.
concept_examples.translation: I want to study abroad.

concept_examples.text: Она поступила в университет в Москве.
concept_examples.translation: She got into the university in Moscow.

concept_examples.text: Мы будем учиться на курсах русского языка.
concept_examples.translation: We will study at Russian language courses.
concept_examples.phonetic: [mɨ ˈbudʲɪm ʊˈt͡ɕit͡sə nə ˈkursəx ˈruskəvə jɪzɨˈka]

concept_examples.text: Стипендия помогает оплатить учёбу.
concept_examples.translation: The scholarship helps pay for studies.

common_error.explanation: The error is mixing Spanish and Russian. Many Spanish speakers translate 'study abroad' literally as 'учить за границу' or use 'в иностранном месте' (incorrect). The correct form is 'учиться за границей' (with the verb 'учиться' and the preposition 'за' + instrumental). Avoid 'учить' (which means 'to teach' or 'to memorize') and use 'учиться' for 'to study' as an academic activity.

levels.label: Глаголы: учиться и поступить
levels.translation: Verbs: to study and to enter

examples.original: Я учусь в университете.
examples.translation: I study at the university.
examples.note: Use 'учиться в + prepositional' to indicate the place of study.

examples.original: Он поступил в аспирантуру.
examples.translation: He entered graduate school.
examples.note: 'Поступить' (perfective) is used for a one-time entry; it is followed by 'в + accusative'.

examples.original: Мы поступаем на курсы.
examples.translation: We are enrolling in the courses.
examples.note: The imperfective 'поступать' expresses a process or repetition.

levels.label: Где учиться: за границей, за рубежом

examples.original: Моя сестра учится за рубежом.
examples.translation: My sister is studying abroad.
examples.note: 'За рубежом' is synonymous with 'за границей', but sometimes more formal.

examples.original: Летом я ездила на стажировку в Германию.
examples.phonetic: [ˈlʲetəm ja ˈjezʲdʲɪlə nə stəʐɨˈrofkʊ v ɡʲɪrˈmanʲɪjʊ]
examples.translation: In the summer, I went to an internship in Germany.
examples.note: 'Стажировка' means professional practice; 'на + accusative' is used to indicate the type of activity.

examples.original: Она получила стипендию на учёбу за границей.
examples.phonetic: [ɐˈna pəɫʊˈt͡ɕiɫə sʲtʲɪˈpʲenʲdʲɪjʊ nə ʊˈt͡ɕɵbʊ zə ˈɡranʲɪt͡sɨj]
examples.translation: She received a scholarship to study abroad.
examples.note: 'Получить' + accusative is used for 'to receive'.

examples.original: Мы участвуем в студенческом обмене.
examples.translation: We are participating in the student exchange.
examples.note: 'Обмен' requires the prepositional case with 'в' to indicate the type of exchange.

title: Путешествия и туризм / Travel and tourism
bridge: In Spanish, to express travel experiences we use the present perfect (he viajado) or the preterite (viajé) depending on the context. In Russian, to talk about life experiences, the perfective aspect in the past is used, but the key distinction is that Russian does not have a direct equivalent of the present perfect; instead, the simple past with perfective aspect (я путешествовал) is used, often accompanied by adverbs like уже (already) or никогда (never). Additionally, Russian distinguishes between determined and undetermined motion in verbs of motion, which does not exist in Spanish. For example, 'ехать' (to go by vehicle, one direction) vs 'ездить' (to go habitually or in both directions). Be careful with this, as Spanish speakers often confuse them.
rule:
To talk about travel and tourism experiences in Russian at B1 level, the main structures used are:
- Motion verbs: ехать/ездить (to go by vehicle) and идти/ходить (to go on foot). 'Ехать' and 'идти' express motion in one direction at the moment. 'Ездить' and 'ходить' express habitual, repeated, or round-trip motion.
- Verbal aspect: perfective (съездить, поехать) for completed or punctual actions; imperfective (ездить, ехать) for processes or habits.
- To express 'I have been in my life', the imperfective or perfective past with frequency adverbs is used: Я уже был в Испании (I have already been to Spain) or Я никогда не был в России (I have never been to Russia).
- Prepositions of place: в (in, inside) with accusative for direction (я еду в Москву) and prepositional for location (я в Москве). In Spanish, the distinction between 'a' and 'en' is similar, but in Russian the case change is mandatory.
- The construction 'у меня есть' to express possession, in travel contexts: у меня есть виза (I have a visa), у меня есть билеты (I have tickets).
- To express duration: preposition 'на' + accusative (на неделю, на два дня).

concept_examples.text: Я уже был в Испании.
concept_examples.translation: I have already been to Spain.

concept_examples.text: Мы ездили в Париж на неделю.
concept_examples.translation: We went to Paris for a week.

concept_examples.text: Он никогда не летал на самолёте.
concept_examples.translation: He has never flown in a plane.

concept_examples.text: Когда ты поедешь в отпуск?
concept_examples.translation: When will you go on vacation?

common_error.wrong: Я ездил в Москву (when trying to say 'I went to Moscow and I'm back' but intending to express an experience).
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because Spanish speakers use the preterite 'fui' for everything, but in Russian, if the action is completed and the person has returned, the perfective aspect of the motion verb with a prefix (съездить) or the verb 'быть' in the past is used. 'Ездил' implies that the action was habitual or repeated, not a one-time experience. To avoid this mistake, think whether the action is a completed experience: then use the perfective aspect.

examples.original: Я еду в аэропорт на такси.
examples.translation: I'm going to the airport by taxi.
examples.note: We use 'еду' (direction now) with the preposition 'на' for transport.

examples.original: Мы обычно ходим в метро.
examples.translation: We usually go by metro.
examples.note: Note that 'ходить' is used for habitual action, not for a specific trip.

examples.original: Ты когда-нибудь летал на вертолёте?
examples.translation: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?
examples.note: We use 'летал' (imperfective) to ask about experience.

examples.original: Я забронировал номер на две ночи.
examples.translation: I have booked a room for two nights.
examples.note: The perfective verb 'забронировал' is used for a completed action and 'на' + accusative for duration.

examples.original: В отеле есть бесплатный Wi-Fi?
examples.translation: Does the hotel have free Wi-Fi?
examples.note: Construction 'у + genitive' or 'есть' for existence. Here we use 'есть' with prepositional.

examples.original: Наш номер выходит на море.
examples.translation: Our room faces the sea.
examples.note: The verb 'выходить' is imperfective and expresses orientation.

examples.original: Поездка была незабываемой!
examples.translation: The trip was unforgettable!
examples.note: Noun 'поездка' (trip by vehicle) + adjective in instrumental case.

examples.original: Мы попробовали местную кухню.
examples.translation: We tried the local cuisine.
examples.note: Use of perfective aspect 'попробовали' for a completed experience.

examples.original: Жаль, что мы не увидели Кремль.
examples.translation: It's a pity we didn't see the Kremlin.
examples.note: Expression 'жаль, что' + negative perfective past.

title: Здоровье и образ жизни / Health and lifestyles
bridge: In Spanish, to talk about habits we use the present indicative and often say 'suelo + infinitive'. In Russian, the verbal aspect (imperfective/perfective) is key: the imperfective is used for habits and routines, while the perfective is for completed actions. Additionally, Russian uses the instrumental case with verbs like 'заниматься' (to practice) and the accusative case with 'пить' (to drink) or 'есть' (to eat). Be careful with the construction 'у меня болит' (I have a pain): the body part is expressed in the nominative and the pronoun in the dative, unlike in Spanish.
rule:
To talk about health and lifestyle in Russian (B1):
- Use the imperfective aspect (present) for routines: 'Я занимаюсь спортом' (I exercise regularly). The perfective is used for specific actions: 'Я позанимался' (I exercised, completed action).
- Verbs that govern specific cases: 'заниматься' (instrumental), 'увлекаться' (instrumental), 'болеть' (accusative for illness: 'болеть гриппом' - instrumental, but 'болеть за...' is not relevant here).
- Expressions of pain: 'у меня болит голова' (I have a headache) - the subject is the body part (nominative), and the possessor is in dative with 'у' + genitive.
- For advice, use the infinitive: 'Надо больше спать' (you need to sleep more), 'Полезно пить воду' (it's good to drink water).
- Frequency: 'часто' (often), 'иногда' (sometimes), 'никогда' (never), 'каждый день' (every day).

concept_examples.text: Я занимaюсь спортом три раза в неделю.
concept_examples.translation: I exercise three times a week.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja zanʲɪˈma.jʉsʲ ˈsportəm trʲi ˈrazə v nʲɪˈdʲelʲʊ]

concept_examples.text: Мне нужно больше спать.
concept_examples.translation: I need to sleep more.

concept_examples.text: У меня болит живот после обеда.
concept_examples.translation: I have a stomachache after lunch.

concept_examples.text: Я стараюсь есть больше овощей и фруктов.
concept_examples.translation: I try to eat more vegetables and fruits.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja stɐˈra.jʉsʲ jesʲtʲ ˈbolʲʂə ɐvɐˈɕːej i ˈfruktəf]

common_error.explanation: Spanish speakers tend to translate 'me duele la cabeza' literally as 'Я болею голову' (verb + direct object). In Russian, pain is expressed with the construction 'у + genitive + болит/болят + nominative subject'. It's important to memorize this structure and not use the verb 'болеть' for pains. Alternatively, you can say 'Голова болит' (subject + verb) without the possessive, but the most common form is 'у меня болит'.

examples.original: Я обычно встаю в семь часов.
examples.translation: I usually get up at seven o'clock.
examples.note: Use of the adverb 'обычно' (usually) and the time construction 'в + number + часов'.

examples.original: Он никогда не курит.
examples.translation: He never smokes.
examples.note: In Russian, with 'никогда' (never) double negation is used: 'никогда не'. Observe the verb in the imperfective.

examples.original: Мы часто ходим в спортзал.
examples.translation: We often go to the gym.
examples.note: The adverb 'часто' (often) and the verb 'ходить' (to go, imperfective) expressing habitual movement.

examples.original: У меня болит горло.
examples.translation: I have a sore throat.
examples.note: Structure 'у меня + болит + nominative'. Learn body parts in the nominative case.

examples.original: Я простудился на прошлой неделе.
examples.translation: I caught a cold last week.
examples.note: Perfective verb 'простудиться' (to catch a cold) indicates a completed action. Used with 'на прошлой неделе' (last week).

examples.original: У него высокая температура.
examples.translation: He has a high fever.
examples.note: Literally 'he has high temperature' - use of 'у' + genitive for possession or state.

examples.original: Мне плохо.
examples.translation: I feel bad.
examples.note: Impersonal construction with dative: 'мне' (to me) + adverb 'плохо' (bad).

examples.original: Тебе надо больше отдыхать.
examples.translation: You need to rest more.
examples.note: Construction 'тебе надо' (you need to) + infinitive. The verb 'отдыхать' is imperfective for habits.

examples.original: Полезно есть кашу по утрам.
examples.translation: It's healthy to eat porridge in the mornings.
examples.note: The adverb 'полезно' (beneficial) + infinitive. 'По утрам' (in the mornings) indicates regularity.

examples.original: Врач сказал пить больше воды.
examples.translation: The doctor said to drink more water.
examples.note: Indirect speech: 'сказал' + infinitive. 'Воды' is partitive genitive after 'больше'.

examples.original: Надо бросить курить и заниматься спортом.
examples.translation: You need to quit smoking and do sports.
examples.note: 'Бросить курить' (to quit smoking) - perfective for a specific action. 'Заниматься' governs the instrumental case: 'спортом'.

title: Обсуждаем отношения и социальную жизнь / Talking about relationships and social life
bridge: In Spanish, to express habitual actions in the past we use the preterite imperfect ('salía', 'veía'). In Russian, this nuance is mainly expressed through verbal aspect: the imperfective (ходил) indicates a habitual or ongoing action, while the perfective (сходил) indicates a completed action. Additionally, Russian uses the instrumental case to express 'with whom' (с друзьями), something that in Spanish is done with the preposition 'con' without a case change. Be careful: there isn't always a direct equivalence between verb tenses, and the use of aspects is more subtle than the simple past/imperfect in Spanish.
rule: To talk about relationships and social life in Russian at level B1, it is essential to master: 1) Verbal aspect: imperfective (ходить, встречаться) for habitual or ongoing actions, perfective (пойти, встретиться) for punctual or completed actions. 2) The instrumental case to indicate company (с друзьями, с семьёй) and also with verbs like быть/стать (быть врачом). 3) The prepositional case (o + prep.) to talk about topics (говорить о работе) and the accusative case for direct objects. 4) Verbs of motion: идти/ходить (to go on foot), ехать/ездить (to go by vehicle), and their prefixes (по-, при-, у-) change the meaning. 5) Expressions of frequent time: часто, иногда, каждый день, раз в неделю. Pay attention to gender and number agreement in adjectives (моя лучшая подруга vs мой лучший друг).

concept_examples.text: Я часто вижусь с друзьями.
concept_examples.translation: I often meet up with my friends.

concept_examples.text: Вчера мы ходили в кино с коллегами.
concept_examples.translation: Yesterday we went to the cinema with colleagues.
concept_examples.phonetic: [fʨɪˈra mɨ xɐˈdʲilʲɪ v kʲɪˈno s kɐlʲˈɛɡəmʲi]

concept_examples.text: Она любит рассказывать о своей семье.
concept_examples.translation: She loves to talk about her family.

concept_examples.text: Мне нравится проводить время с моей девушкой.
concept_examples.translation: I like to spend time with my girlfriend.
concept_examples.phonetic: [mnʲe ˈnravʲɪtsə prɐˈvɐdʲitʲ ˈvrʲemʲə s ˈmojɪj ˈdʲevʊʂkəj]

common_error.explanation: The main error is the omission of the pronominal verb (встречаюсь) and the incorrect use of cases: 'с' requires the instrumental case (с подругой, not 'с подруга') and the possessive must agree (с моей). In Spanish, 'encontrarse con alguien' is pronominal and uses 'con', but there is no case change. Remember that in Russian, verbs like встречаться, видеться, расставаться are reflexive and require 'с' + instrumental.

examples.original: Давай пойдём в кафе сегодня вечером?
examples.translation: Shall we go to a café this evening?
examples.note: Use of 'давай' + perfective verb in the future to suggest a joint action.

examples.original: Ты свободен в субботу?
examples.translation: Are you free on Saturday?
examples.note: The short adjective 'свободен' (masculine) is used to express availability.

examples.original: Хочешь пойти на день рождения к Сергею?
examples.phonetic: [ˈxotɕɪʂ pɐjˈtʲi nə dʲenʲ rɐˈʐdʲenʲɪjə k sʲɪrˈɡʲejʊ]
examples.translation: Do you want to go to Serguéi's birthday?
examples.note: The construction 'к + dative' to indicate the person whose house you are going to.

examples.original: Не могу, у меня уже планы.
examples.translation: I can't, I already have plans.
examples.note: The expression 'у меня' is used for possession in Russian, not 'yo tengo'.

examples.original: Она мой лучший друг.
examples.translation: She is my best friend.
examples.note: Grammatical gender does not match the sex: 'друг' is masculine, so it is 'мой лучший друг' even if referring to a woman (though colloquially 'моя лучшая подруга' is used).

examples.original: Мы с ним знакомы ещё со школы.
examples.phonetic: [mɨ s nʲim znɐˈkomɨ ɪˈɕːɵ s ˈʂko.lɨ]
examples.translation: I've known him since school.
examples.note: The construction 'с + instrumental' means 'since' when used with 'знакомы'.

examples.original: У нас хорошие отношения со свекровью.
examples.translation: We have a good relationship with our mother-in-law.
examples.note: 'Отношения' is plural and is used with 'с' + instrumental.

examples.original: Мы встречаемся уже год.
examples.translation: We've been dating for a year.
examples.note: The verb 'встречаться' is imperfective and indicates a romantic relationship.

examples.original: На прошлой неделе мы были на свадьбе у кузины.
examples.phonetic: [nə ˈproʂləj nʲɪˈdʲelʲe mɨ ˈbɨlʲɪ nə ˈsvadʲbʲe u kʊˈzʲinɨ]
examples.translation: Last week we were at my cousin's wedding.
examples.note: 'у + genitive' to indicate possession or relationship with a person.

examples.original: На вечеринке было много людей.
examples.translation: There were a lot of people at the party.
examples.note: 'Людей' is the genitive plural of 'люди' and is used after 'много'.

examples.original: Мы познакомились на концерте.
examples.translation: We met at a concert.
examples.note: Perfective verb 'познакомиться' for a punctual action.

examples.original: Он пригласил меня на юбилей своей бабушки.
examples.phonetic: [on prʲɪɡlɐˈsʲil mʲɪˈnʲa nə jʉbʲɪˈlʲej svɐˈjɛj ˈbabʊʂkʲɪ]
examples.translation: He invited me to his grandmother's anniversary.
examples.note: Use of 'своей' (reflexive possessive) to refer to the subject (he).

title: Давать краткую презентацию / Giving a brief presentation
bridge: In Spanish, when giving a brief presentation, we often use connectors like 'first', 'then', 'in conclusion' and impersonal structures. In Russian, aside from connectors (сначала, потом, в заключение), verbal aspect (perfective/imperfective) is crucial: completed actions use the perfective aspect, while ongoing or habitual actions use the imperfective. Additionally, word order is more flexible, but emphasis is marked through intonation and position rather than articles (Russian has no articles). Spanish speakers often transfer the structure 'me gustaría hablar de' literally, but in Russian constructions with verbs like 'рассказать' (to tell) and the prepositional case for the topic are used.
rule: To present a topic in Russian at B1 level, introductory phrases like 'Я хочу рассказать о...' (I want to talk about...) are used, where 'о' is followed by the prepositional case. Temporal connectors include 'сначала' (first), 'потом' (then), 'затем' (after), 'наконец' (finally). To express opinions, 'я думаю' (I think) or 'я считаю' (I consider) are used, followed by a clause with the verb in the appropriate aspect. To conclude: 'В заключение...' (In conclusion...). It is common to use the imperfective aspect to describe the development of the presentation (рассказывать = to tell, ongoing process) and the perfective for the result (рассказать = to tell, completed action). Personal pronouns are often omitted when the verb already indicates the person, but in formal presentations they can be included for emphasis. Possessive adjectives must agree in gender, number, and case with the noun.

concept_examples.text: Я хочу рассказать о моей поездке в Москву.
concept_examples.translation: I want to talk about my trip to Moscow.
concept_examples.phonetic: [ja xɐˈʧu rəskɐˈzatʲ ɐ ˈmojɪj pɐˈjɛtkʲe v mɐˈskvu]

concept_examples.text: Сначала я покажу фотографии.
concept_examples.translation: First, I will show some photos.

concept_examples.text: Потом мы обсудим основные моменты.
concept_examples.translation: Then we will discuss the main points.

concept_examples.text: В заключение я отвечу на вопросы.
concept_examples.translation: In conclusion, I will answer the questions.

common_error.wrong: Я хочу hablar sobre мой поездка.
common_error.correct: Я хочу рассказать о моей поездке.
common_error.correct_alt: Я хочу рассказать про свою поездку.
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because the student mixes Spanish and Russian (code-switching) and does not apply the prepositional case correctly. Additionally, they use the Spanish infinitive 'hablar' instead of the Russian verb 'рассказать' (to tell), which is more natural in this context. The preposition 'о' (about) requires the prepositional case: 'о моей поездке' (about my trip). It is also common to forget the agreement of the possessive adjective 'моей' (feminine singular in prepositional case). To avoid this, it is important to memorize the verb 'рассказать' with its prepositional case structure: 'рассказать о + prepositional' and practice the declension of possessive adjectives.

examples.original: Меня зовут Анна, и я расскажу о нашей компании.
examples.phonetic: [mʲɪˈnʲa zɐˈvut ˈannə, i ja rəskɐˈʐu ɐ ˈnaʂɨj kɐmˈpanʲɪɪ]
examples.translation: My name is Anna and I will talk about our company.
examples.note: Use of 'меня зовут' (my name is) and the perfective future of 'рассказать' (I will talk) to indicate a completed action.

examples.original: Моя презентация состоит из трёх частей.
examples.translation: My presentation consists of three parts.
examples.note: Use of 'состоит' (consists) with the genitive 'из трёх частей' (of three parts).

examples.original: Сначала я расскажу о целях проекта.
examples.translation: First, I will talk about the project goals.
examples.note: The adverb 'сначала' (first) is a typical connector to start the structure.

examples.original: Во-первых, наша цель – увеличить продажи.
examples.translation: Firstly, our goal is to increase sales.
examples.note: The connector 'во-первых' (firstly) is very useful for listing points. The dash (—) in Russian is used to link subject and predicate.

examples.original: Во-вторых, мы уже начали работать над этим.
examples.translation: Secondly, we have already started working on this.
examples.note: Use of the perfective aspect 'начали' (we started) to indicate a completed action. The adverb 'уже' (already) with perfective indicates a result.

examples.original: Кроме того, мы планируем расширение на рынок Латинской Америки.
examples.phonetic: [ˈkromʲɪ ˈtovə, mɪ plɐˈnʲirʊjɪm rɐˈʂɨrʲɪnʲɪje nə ˈrɨnək lɐˈtʲinskəj ɐˈmʲɛrʲɪkʲɪ]
examples.translation: In addition, we plan to expand into the Latin American market.
examples.note: The connector 'кроме того' (in addition) adds information. 'Расширение' (expansion) governs the accusative 'на рынок' (into the market).

examples.original: Наконец, мы должны обсудить бюджет.
examples.translation: Finally, we must discuss the budget.
examples.note: 'Наконец' (finally) indicates the conclusion of the main section. The modal verb 'должны' (must) combines with the infinitive.

examples.original: В заключение, я хочу подвести итоги.
examples.translation: In conclusion, I want to summarize the points.
examples.note: The expression 'в заключение' (in conclusion) is used to close. The perfective infinitive 'подвести итоги' (to summarize, literally 'to bring to a conclusion the results') is a fixed collocation.

examples.original: Если у вас есть вопросы, я с удовольствием отвечу.
examples.phonetic: [ˈjeslʲɪ u vas jesʲtʲ vɐˈprosɨ, ja s‿ʊdɐˈvolʲstvʲɪjɪm ɐtˈvʲɛʧu]
examples.translation: If you have any questions, I will be happy to answer them.
examples.note: The conditional construction 'если...' (if...) is common in presentations. 'С удовольствием' (with pleasure) is a fixed expression.

examples.original: Спасибо за внимание!
examples.translation: Thank you for your attention!
examples.note: A typical polite formula used at the end. 'За' + accusative (внимание) indicates the cause.
